subject: Preflight: Node orchestration and soft hold request for Penumbra POC
messages:
From: Nora Park <nora@penumbra.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2024 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity ask for upcoming POC (timing + hold)

Hi David,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency numbers. We need to finalize a short runway commitment for a customer-facing POC. High level: 8 A100-class GPUs immediately for a 2-week spike (April 29 - May 12) and the option to scale to 32 GPUs across a dedicated pool in early June if initial metrics look good.

Before we lock a PO we need a soft hold or availability confirmation so our SREs can coordinate networking/config with minimal risk. Can Redwood place a provisional hold on the requested capacity and share any constraints (node affinity, minimum scheduling lead time, cooling/thermal notes)? I can share a draft PO and the feature checklist.

Attached: penumbra_capacity_estimate.xlsx (quick numbers).

Best,
Nora
Nora Park
Head of Cloud Ops, Penumbra AI
Procurement: procurement@penumbra.ai

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Nora Park <nora@penumbra.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2024 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity ask for upcoming POC (timing + hold)

Nora — thanks for the clear numbers and the file. We can do a provisional hold but need to align on a couple of internal constraints and an explicit Mutual Action Plan (MAP).

Summary from our side:
- Immediate spike: 8x A100-equivalent nodes (best-effort, shared pool) for Apr 29–May 12.
- Scale target: ability to reserve 32x GPUs in a dedicated pool by first week of June (ideally with 72 hours notice once you signal go).

Requests from Penumbra for the MAP:
1) Confirm exact window for Apr spike and any blackout times.
2) Indicate whether you can accept split-region placement (we prefer single-region but can accommodate multi-region if you need redundancy).
3) Sign the PO draft and a short SLO appendix for the POC (we’ll attach template).

Operational notes: Ben will scope whether we can do a soft hold in the shared pool vs. creating a dedicated small pool. Karthik — please comment on thermal/affinity constraints and whether 32 GPUs requires a hardware mix (A100 vs A800) that could affect lead time. Monica — I’ll need the MAP and internal CS checklist to share with Nora.

I’ve attached a blank MAP template and the draft PO you can use to move quickly. If Penumbra signs and confirms the spike window, we’ll open a provisional hold ticket and push to Ops for node tagging.

-David

--
David Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Nora Park <nora@penumbra.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Apr 2024 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity ask for upcoming POC (timing + hold)

Looping in Ops notes and feasibility. Short version: we can do the Apr 29 spike but with controls so production customers aren’t impacted.

Operational constraints and proposed controls:
- Soft hold mode: mark capacity as "provisional-reserve" for the Apr 29–May 12 window. This prevents allocation for other new late-stage commitments but still allows short preemptible bursts for internal test jobs if needed.
- Node mix: 8x A100-equivalent is fine from inventory; however, moving to 32x in June requires us to either: 1) convert a slice of the dedicated pool to your tenancy (preferred) or 2) pre-assign 32x across heterogeneous hardware (A100/A800) with potential perf variance.
- Scheduling lead: for a dedicated small pool we need 7 business days lead to pin nodes and run networking prep (VPC peering, IPs). For best latency guarantees, request single-region placement (we can do us-west-2).
- Thermal/placement: Karthik to confirm if any additional rack-level affinity is needed. If Penumbra needs contiguous racks, lead time may increase to 14 business days.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Penumbra provides signed PO draft + final spike window by EOD Monday (Apr 22).
2) We create provisional-reserve ticket internally and tag the nodes as "PEN-POC-PENDING".
3) Share the MAP and perform a quick network checklist call.

I’m attaching the Ops readiness checklist (stub) — Nora, please add your SRE contact for the network call.

-Ben

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Nora Park <nora@penumbra.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Apr 2024 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity ask for upcoming POC (timing + hold)

Thanks — quick technical clarifications from infra:
- 8x spike: no special rack affinity required; we can pull from the shared pool in us-west-2. Node tagging will be sufficient for provisioning the spike.
- 32x dedicated pool: if Penumbra wants contiguous racks to avoid cross-switch hop for the model’s KV cache behavior, that will push the timeline to ~10 business days to reserve and certify. Otherwise heterogeneous spread is doable in 5–7 business days.
- Quantization/throughput: if you expect consistent 32-GPU sustained batching, recommend Q4 quantization profile we discussed — that will reduce thermal churn and improve density. We can pre-stage the quantization profile on the reserved nodes once you confirm the scaling decision.

Operational asks for Penumbra:
1) Confirm single-region preference (yes/no).
2) Provide SRE point-of-contact for the network/peering call.
3) Signal whether contiguous racks are required.

David — I’ve created internal ticket INF-4721 to request the provisional-reserve state and added a note to flag the lead-time based on contiguous-rack requirement. Ben — please convert INF-4721 into a hold if Penumbra signs and returns the PO.

-Karthik
